Staff reading this section are responsible for following it carefully and using it to give calm, accurate help to travelers and crews.

Companion Animal Travel Desk: Service and Handling Standards

This section sets the basic rules for handling companion animal travel requests, crate checks, and follow-up support so every traveler gets steady, respectful service.

Keep your tone warm and practical from the first contact, whether you are speaking with the traveler, a crew member, or a station partner. Confirm the travel details, check the animal type against the current acceptance rules, and make sure the crate, documents, and routing all match before anything is accepted. If a traveler brings up a missing crate or a damaged one, log the report right away and guide them through the next steps without sounding rushed or doubtful. <<FACT F118>> Make sure the traveler knows the claim process is being handled and that the desk will stay available for further help.

When reviewing crate fit, treat each animal case with care and look for enough room to stand, turn, and lie down comfortably. For a rabbit booking, measure the crate against the required standard before approval. <<FACT F070>> If the crate does not meet the standard, explain the issue plainly and suggest a proper correction before travel can be confirmed.

For reptile travel, do not assume the booking can move forward until the age rule has been checked against the current file. <<FACT F078>> If the record is incomplete, pause the request and ask for the missing support instead of guessing. Keep all notes clear and neutral, and share only what the crew needs to complete safe handling. If a pet name is used in the file, copy it exactly as provided.

Stay prompt, respectful, and steady in every reply, and keep the traveler informed as the case moves through review. If you need help with a special case, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at Aurelia Skyways.
